cases.note: logic_op/or/single-result: both operands succeed contributes one element
modules:
package test
import future.keywords.or

# Comprehension makes cardinality observable: a broken `or` that ran
# both operands and emitted two outer successes would yield [1, 1].
p := [1 |
  true or true
]

cases.note: logic_op/or/single-result: nested or, all branches succeed contributes one element
logic_op/or/single-result: inside iterating comprehension, one entry per outer binding
modules:
package test
import future.keywords.or

p := [i |
  i := input.xs[_]
  i > 0 or i != 0 # if lhs/rhs both contributed a result, we'd get duplicates in the array
]
